wrong.A gap up through the flag top: A gap is a trigger event. It says nothing about tight closes inside the flag.

questions.why: Closes that stay tight each week. Our card calls tight weekly closes through the flag the A+ tightness cue. That sits on top of the gate: the last 5 closes before the trigger within 10%. IBD's JDSU flag shows why: wild weekly ranges, relatively tight closes. Light volume grades the flag's volume, and a gap is a trigger event. Neither is the tightness cue.
questions.lesson_line: Judge a flag by where it closes, not by its wicks.
questions.simple: Tight weekly closes, because our card calls them the A+ cue, even when the weekly ranges look wide.

reasons: the A+ cue rests on one card line (c50)
IBD's JDSU example supports the closes-over-ranges idea

questions.q: We skip a high tight flag when sales and earnings are not growing.
questions.why: False. Growing sales and earnings, or a real catalyst, are preferred but not required. The chart comes first.
questions.lesson_line: Preferred, not required. The chart comes first.
questions.simple: False, because growing sales and earnings are preferred but not required, and the chart comes first.

reasons: +2 rests on the owner's rulebook (D40, the chart comes first)

questions.q: What does our rule say?
questions.story: Every chart test is met: a double in seven weeks off a quiet base, a tight flag and a trigger. Sales growth stalled last quarter. A big new contract drove the pole.
choices: Buy it; the chart comes first
Pass; sales must be growing
Wait until sales turn up
Buy it, but at half size

wrong.Pass; sales must be growing: Growth is preferred, not required. A real catalyst counts, and the chart comes first.
wrong.Wait until sales turn up: Waiting on sales is not a rule. The chart sets the entry.
wrong.Buy it, but at half size: No rule halves the size for a sales dip. The size comes from the stop, and a real catalyst drove the pole.

questions.answer: Buy it; the chart comes first
questions.why: Buy it; the chart comes first. Growing sales and earnings, or a real catalyst, are preferred but not required. Here a big new contract drove the pole, and every chart test is met.
questions.lesson_line: Growth is preferred, never required. The chart comes first.
questions.simple: Buy it, because growth is preferred but not required and a real contract drove the pole.

deeper.trap: Treating preferred as required. The rule asks for growing sales and earnings, or a real catalyst, and the chart still comes first. A big new contract is a real change in the business, so the setup keeps its place. Skipping a clean chart over one soft quarter would be a rule we do not have.

reasons: +2 rests on the owner's rulebook (D40, preferred not required)

questions.q: You buy at 100.00 and the flag low is 88.00. How far under your fill is a stop at the flag low, in percent?
questions.why: The fill minus the stop, divided by the fill: (100.00 minus 88.00) divided by 100.00 is 12.0%. Our stop usually sits within about 3% of the buy, so the flag low is about four times too wide. It kills the idea but is not the stop.
questions.lesson_line: The flag low ends the idea. The stop is much closer.
questions.simple: A stop at the flag low would sit 12.0% under the fill, far wider than the usual 3%.

reasons: computed key
rests on the owner's rulebook (A13)

wrong.13.6%: That divides by the stop. Divide by the fill.
wrong.88.0%: That is the stop as a share of the fill, not the gap.
wrong.120.0%: Decimal slip: one place too far right.

questions.q: Bulkowski's own stop for a high tight flag is the bottom of the flag.
questions.why: True. Bulkowski says to use the bottom of the congestion area formed in the flag phase as the stop price. Ours is different: a few cents under the day's low. For us the flag low is the line that kills the idea, not the stop.
questions.lesson_line: Bulkowski stops at the flag bottom. Ours is a few cents under the day's low.
questions.simple: True, because Bulkowski puts the stop at the bottom of the flag, but our stop is much closer, under the day's low.

deeper.trap: Copying the textbook stop. Bulkowski's stop is the bottom of the flag, which can sit far more than 3% under the buy. Our rulebook says the stop usually sits within about 3% of the buy. A flag-low stop would force a much smaller size or no trade, so the flag low stays the line that kills the idea.

reasons: +3 the key rests on one cited fact (Bulkowski's stop locations page)

questions.q: Bought at 60.00, stop at 57.50. What is 1R, in dollars a share?
questions.why: One R is the risk you take on the trade, the fill minus the stop. Here that is 60.00 minus 57.50, which is 2.50 a share. A 3R winner is three times that.

questions.q: On our card, does this flag pass the fast-averages check?
questions.story: A stock nearly doubled in seven weeks, then paused 12 sessions a little under its high. One close in that pause sat under the 21-day EMA. Today it trades through the high.
choices: No, the card allows zero such closes
Yes, one dip is fine above the 50-day
Yes, if both averages are rising now
No, it paused too long to count
questions.answer: No, the card allows zero such closes
questions.why: No. On our card, no close in the flag may sit below the 21-day EMA. At the trigger, price must also be above a rising 10-day and a rising 21-day EMA. Rising means higher than 5 sessions ago. Both halves count.
questions.lesson_line: On our card, the flag rides rising fast averages and never closes under the 21-day EMA.

wrong.Yes, one dip is fine above the 50-day: The 50-day is a separate check on our card. The flag line is no close under the 21-day EMA.
wrong.Yes, if both averages are rising now: Rising averages are only half the line. Our card also wants no flag close under the 21-day EMA.
wrong.No, it paused too long to count: Our card allows a pause of 5 to 30 sessions. A 12-session pause sits inside that.

questions.q: By our rule, may you move the stop to breakeven now?
questions.story: You bought a high tight flag breakout. It is now up 2R. You have not sold any shares yet.
choices: Yes, that is inside our window
No, only after the first trim
No, it must wait for 5R or more
Yes, but only on heavy volume
questions.answer: Yes, that is inside our window
questions.why: Yes. Our rule moves the stop to breakeven between 2R and 5R, ideally. 2R already sits inside the window, so the move is allowed now. The stop only moves up, never down.
questions.lesson_line: Breakeven goes in between 2R and 5R, ideally. It does not wait for a sale.

wrong.No, only after the first trim: The window opens at 2R. It does not wait for the first sale.
wrong.No, it must wait for 5R or more: 5R is the late end of the window, not its start. It opens at 2R.
wrong.Yes, but only on heavy volume: Our rule ties breakeven to how far the trade is up in R, not to volume.

questions.simple: Yes, because our rule allows breakeven anywhere from 2R to 5R, and this trade is at 2R.

reasons: +2 rests on the owner's rulebook (B19, breakeven at 2R to 5R ideally) and the card's default (at the first trim)
